messages:
kevin: Heads up — saw steady memory growth on a long-chat repro (10k tokens) after ~300s. Heap shows lots of KVPage objects not freed. Suspect page boundary metadata not being cleared on eviction.

maria: can you paste the repro command and the small heap diff?

kevin: repro: `./run_local_server --model redwood-1-7b --kv-page-size 4mb --max-context 12000`
logs snippet:
```
I0324 12:15:41.123 evict.cc:214] evicting page_id=402 start_token=8192 end_token=12287 owner=req-9
I0324 12:15:41.124 kvpage.cc:98] page 402 reused for req-12 without clearing prev_owner
I0324 12:15:42.001 cache.cc:477] stale_block detected: page=402 block_offset=64 prev_owner=req-9
```

kevin: note the "reused for req-12 without clearing prev_owner" — that prev_owner pointer stays and content from req-9 appears in subsequent outputs (rarely).

ajay: that aligns with something I saw — when eviction splits a page we create a fragment record but we don't zero the fragment->last_token when we splice. That can make `get_kv_range()` return an overlapping range.

sasha: can we assert that on allocate we always set `fragment->last_token = INVALID` and `owner = NONE`? Simple but might mask deeper alignment bug.

kevin: posted quick struct dump of KVPage header:
```
struct KVPageHeader {
  uint64_t page_id;
  uint32_t start_token; // token index of first KV pair
  uint32_t end_token;   // past-the-end token index
  uint32_t owner_req_id; // request id that pinned this page
  uint16_t frag_count;
  uint16_t reserved;
};
```

maria: perf-bot uploaded pprof: `/pprof/1778098765/heap`
perf-bot: heap summary: "KVPage (x432)  -> retained 52.3MB; average live_size 125KB; stack: evict.cc:214, alloc.cc:48"

ajay: interesting — evict path shows we sometimes set `start_token` based on a stale offset variable (`last_seen_token`) that isn't atomically updated for concurrent evictions. Race between split + reuse could produce wrong alignment.

kevin: repro more deterministic if you do concurrent streams: `ab -n 50 -c 10` style client calling streaming API with variable ctx lengths. Then you see garbled tokens in ~1/2000 requests.

sasha: I sketched a small fix: on page recycle do `memset(&header, 0, sizeof(header)); header.page_id = new_id; header.start_token = new_start;` then publish. Also add an assert in debug builds: verify no owner present when reused.

maria: +1 for the aggressive zeroing. Also add a unit test: allocate page, write two small fragments, evict first fragment leaving a hole, reuse page and assert no cross-request read from old fragment.

ajay: we should also add a perf regression check — zeroing could be slightly more costly on hot path. Add microbench `kv_reuse_zeroing` and compare. If overhead > 1% we can optimize by only clearing small header fields instead of full memset.

kevin: I'll open a PR with both the memset and the unit test. Assigning to me for now. I'll run canary on staging with stress harness for 6 hours.

maria: thanks. also add telemetry metric `kv.page_reuse_stale_reads` increment if we detect owner mismatch at runtime — helps detect any remaining cases in prod.

perf-bot: perf test queued: `kv_reuse_zeroing` against baseline (runs: 1000) — results expected in ~30m.

kevin: putting a TODO: audit other places where fragments are split (`split_fragment_at_offset`) — make sure they don't copy stale `last_token`.

sasha: if canary looks good, let's ship as a patch release. If not, revert and we have rollback plan: pin to older alloc behavior and disable reuse for pages > 1MB.

kevin: thanks all — I'll post PR link when ready and paste staging logs.
